prediction: One NFS MW run at 234b269b99 with HAKUX_APU_VOICELOG=1 (source-side log in vp.c, off by default). The instrument hashes every 32-sample source block the VP reads, keyed by its address, and calls a loud block stale when its hash equals that address's on the previous read. Claim A (the brief's): the VP-side stale share of the sounding voice(s) agrees with the output-side lag-2400 share of the same run within 5 points. Agreement places the replay at the VP's read of guest memory: the VP read a block the guest had not rewritten since its previous lap. Disagreement (VP share near 0 while the output shows >= 5%) places it upstream, in content the guest itself repeated into fresh memory, and then the fix is not in the VP. Claim M (the mechanism, one of): H-A' (P 0.5): the music voice is a looping buffer of 2400 samples (EBO 2399, or a multiple), the scanner shows the guest's writes arriving at a steady cadence, stale runs begin during VP bursts (the c<block> column jumps by tens of blocks within a few ms) with blk_wr_age about one lap (40-60 ms) and sslrep 0; H-B (P 0.25): sslrep > 0 or sslempty on the sounding voice, or stale runs while the scanner's write head is well ahead of the CBO, or CBO moves no PIO wrote; H-C/guest repeat (P 0.2): A fails as above, or gaps in the guest's scan writes line up with stale runs while the VP runs steadily; other (P 0.05). Expected output share 8-30% (the build now carries nfsdefault1011's NFS switches, so 15.1% is not assumed). P(A) 0.6. Claim W (Addendum 2, lane.local's): replay starts coincide with a guest voice update in the wait before the VP burst they start in. Read from the sec lines' bx table (loudest voice; 'update' = any guest FE method on it, VOICE_LOCK included, between the end of the last VP frame and the burst's first): W holds if >= 80% of bursts with a stale start followed an update AND that share exceeds the share for bursts without a stale start by >= 20 points. P(W) 0.25: a game that sets volume or polls position under VOICE_LOCK each video frame addresses the voice in nearly every ~40 ms wait, which makes 'coincide' near 100% in both rows and the lift near 0; that outcome is reported as 'not separated', not as support. Claim B (bql): the APU thread's non-throttle wait (gapx, an upper bound on bql_lock) is < 2 ms per second median, so bql is not where the wait goes, P 0.7. Claim O (H-A' at the source): for stale starts on the loudest voice, 32*boff - ahead (VP samples into the burst minus the guest's lead at the burst's start) is within +/-256 samples in >= 60% of paired bursts, P 0.45.

legs.V (instrument, else VOID): logcat carries 'apuvoice on:' once, >= 150 'apuvoice sec' lines, and the pulled capture is >= 150 s of 48 kHz stereo. Dropped counts are reported; > 20% of event lines dropped in the loud windows makes leg M's timing read 'partial', not void.
legs.A (agreement): |VP stale share (pooled stale/(stale+fresh) over the voice lines of the top voice by loud blocks, all seconds) - output lag-2400 share (replay_share.py)| <= 5 points. Reported per 30 s window too; judged on the whole run.
legs.M (mechanism): Named in NOTES.md with the stale, scan, voice and sslsw lines that show it, per the claim's table. Not a number.
legs.P (pacing, reported): vpframes per second (1500 is real time), the lead range, bursts and maxgap from the sec lines.
legs.W (Addendum 2, update in the wait): voiceread.py leg W, 'top voice' row: share of stale-start bursts after an update >= 80% and lift >= 20 points. Also reported: the any-voice VOICE_LOCK row, the voice-lock stall totals, and wfe/wlock/wlockall on stale lines.
legs.B (bql bound): voiceread.py leg W, 'APU wait outside throttle' median < 2 ms/s. If not, the bound is too loose to clear bql and an apu.c.patch build times bql_lock directly.
legs.O (outrun): voiceread.py leg W, 'stale start vs guest head': |32*boff - ahead| <= 256 for >= 60% of pairs (pairs need both burst lines; the budget drops some).
